title: Time and Physical Geometry
version: The Journal of Philosophy 64(8) (1967), pp. 240-247. JSTOR-scan PDF (weebly-hosted, cover sheet confirms Vol. 64, No. 8, pp. 240-247, stable URL jstor.org/stable/2024493); full text extracted this run, printed page numbers visible in scan (240-247). Same public copy the predecessor lane used (riv-putnam-1967 at predecessor commit 1fb23fd).
relevance: Primary anchor for Contract E (whole-history eternalism): thesis (1) foil, assumptions i-ii, Principle III and its three restricting clauses, reality transfer via transitive closure with 'enough observers', tenseless-existence coextension, anti-absolute-simultaneity clause.
limits: Research quotation only; OCR spacing normalized without wording change. The future-contingent truth-value section (pp. 243-246) is recorded as Putnam's separate, stronger argument, distinct from the reality-transfer route.
locator: thesis (1) p. 240; assumptions i-ii p. 240; Principle III p. 241 with tenseless-language clause ('understood as stated in "tenseless" language, except for the indexical terms') and coordinate-independence clause p. 241; transfer argument pp. 241-243; concession 'Strictly speaking, I showed only that some future things are real' p. 246; 'all future things are real ("things" here includes "events")' p. 246; transitive closure and 'enough observers' p. 246; Lorentz-invariance/absolute-simultaneity clause p. 246; tenseless existence = 'will exist, or has existed, or exists right now' and real/existence coextension p. 246; 'solved by physics and not by philosophy' p. 247; 'no longer any philosophical problems about Time' p. 247
assumptions: Man-on-street thesis (1) as foil; i. I-now real; ii. another possibly moving observer real; III. no privileged observers, for tenseless coordinate-independent physical R
conclusion: Putnam's claims: on natural choices of R future and past things are real though not existing now; 'real' coextensive with tenseless existence; a privileged-frame reading would define an absolute simultaneity
proof_status: Argumentative essay, first-hand verified this run; the project's audit (found-putnam, knowledge/foundations) holds that Lorentz kinematics alone does not entail the conclusion: Principle III is a bridge premise
open_questions: Whether Principle III's neutrality constraint coincides with Stein 1991's automorphism-invariance condition (bridge-premises lane)

title: How to teach special relativity
version: Reprint in 'Speakable and Unspeakable in Quantum Mechanics' (CUP 1987; 2004 edition with Aspect introduction per scan title page), pp. 67-80; publicly hosted PDF read this run; printed page footers 77-78 verified at the quoted passage.
relevance: Primary anchor for Contract G's Lorentzian preferred-frame premise: a real rest state defined by the aether that the laws conspire to hide; Bell's explicit separation of physics from philosophy of the Lorentzian approach.
limits: Opening, Bell-conflict discussion, and closing sections inspected this run; the essay's dynamical details not re-read. Scan quality good; wording of the key passage checked in two passes.
locator: printed pp. 77-78: 'Lorentz, on the other hand, preferred the view that there is indeed a state of real rest, defined by the "aether", even though the laws of physics conspire to prevent us identifying it experimentally. The facts of physics do not oblige us to accept one philosophy rather than the other. And we need not accept Lorentz's philosophy to accept a Lorentzian pedagogy.'; p. 78: 'the laws of physics in any one reference frame account for all physical phenomena, including the observations of moving observers'
assumptions: Lorentz-invariant laws formulated in one frame; moving observers and instruments derived from those laws
conclusion: Single-frame formulation accounts for all appearances; preference for a real rest frame is philosophical, not experimentally forced
open_questions: Whether a Bell-style real rest frame plus Broad growth yields a coherent relativistic GBT (Contract G), and what Earman 2008's non-cheating objection does to it

title: Scientific Thought
version: London: Kegan Paul, Trench, Trubner / New York: Harcourt, Brace, 1923. Internet Archive item scientificthough00broauoft (University of Toronto scan); djvu.txt OCR read this run (normalized double spacing). Running headers 'TIME AND CHANGE 67' and garbled '( )8 SCIENTIFIC THOUGHT' [= 68] frame the key passages, matching the predecessor's printed pp. 66-68 locators.
relevance: Primary anchor for Contract G (growing block): reality of present+past, future 'simply nothing at all', sum total of existence always increasing (sense as well as order), Becoming as the third kind of change on which the other two depend; growing life-history persistence picture.
limits: Only the Ch. 2 time-and-change region (printed pp. 66-68) inspected this run; rest of book unread. OCR garbles noted: 'Similarlv' for 'Similarly', page-number header of p. 68; wording of quoted clauses otherwise verbatim after whitespace normalization.
locator: printed p. 66: 'accepts the reality of the present and the past, but holds that the future is simply nothing at all'; 'A Specious Present of mine is just the last thin slice that has joined up to my life-history'; 'other slices have been tacked on to my life-history'; pp. 66-67: 'Nothing has happened to the present by becoming past except that fresh slices of existence have been added to the total history of the world. The past is thus as real as the present.'; p. 67: 'The sum total of existence is always increasing, and it is this which gives the time-series a sense as well as an order.'; 'A moment t is later than a moment t' if the sum total of existence at t includes the sum total of existence at t' together with something more.'; pp. 67-68: 'a complete analysis of the qualitative changes of things is found to involve the coming into existence of events'; 'Let us call the third kind of change Becoming.'
assumptions: Absolute (Newtonian) time order; events as particulars that come into existence
conclusion: Growth of the sum total of existence grounds temporal direction and underlies attribute-change and pastward change
proof_status: Philosophical argument, first-hand verified this run; no formal theorem claimed
open_questions: Whether Earman 2008's 'non-cheating' objection blocks the Newtonian realization (gate: Earman PDF absent from this worktree)

title: Replies to Critics
version: Disputatio Vol. XIII, No. 63, December 2021, pp. 445-494, doi 10.2478/disp-2021-0026, BIBLID [0873-626X (2021) 63; pp. 445-94], CC BY-NC-ND 3.0. Open-access Sciendo PDF read this run. (The predecessor relied on the future-truth-rivals coordinator lane record; this run verifies section 8 first-hand.)
relevance: Source of the later-grounding clause for Contract B and the bivalent-G hybrid: distinguishes the currently-existing explanandum-fact from the not-currently-existing explanans-fact; answers Dorato-Hoefer's 'only superficially distinct from eternalism' charge; concedes the coherence of Bohmian-style preferred-order physics.
limits: Section 8 (pp. 482-485) verified verbatim this run; sections 6-7 (Dyke, Miller exchanges, pp. 457-465) inspected in the same fetch; remaining sections not read this run.
locator: p. 482: Torre exchange on existential indeterminism; pp. 482-483: Mars-outposts example, 'requirement on truth: where phi is a sentence that is true now, it should hold that, sometimes, there are things such that phi is true now because those things exist then'; pp. 483-484: 'In R, the explanandum-fact is the fact that Q is true now. Ex hypothesi that fact currently exists. By contrast, the present truth of R does not imply that there currently exists a corresponding explanans-fact'; p. 484: 'We do not think so' against 'only superficially distinct from eternalism'; 'some of the currently existing facts ... do so only courtesy of what will but may not yet exist'; p. 485: Bohmian concession 'we have nothing to say against it'
assumptions: NTC grounding framework; bivalence for future contingents; Aristotelian truth-because schema without robust facts (Horwich)
conclusion: Present truth about the future does not require present existence of its future explanans; GBT with later grounding is not thereby eternalism, by the authors' lights; absolute-simultaneity metaphysics is not incoherent, only possibly physically otiose
proof_status: Authors' reply; first-hand verified this run; arguments accepted here as their claims, not independently established
open_questions: Whether their extended logic admits the Contract-L one-point instance (needs NTC chs. 1-5, gate)
